title: VAMR: Multi-Question Agentic Reasoning for Efficient Long-Form Video Understanding
abstract: arXiv:2610.11171v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Long-form video understanding often involves multiple questions about different aspects of the same recording. Yet existing video agents typically process each question through an isolated tool-use trajectory. This repeatedly restarts video exploration and memory construction, missing opportunities to acquire evidence jointly and progressively build a shared understanding that supports the complete question set. We introduce \textbf{VAMR} (\textbf{V}ideo \textbf{A}gent for \textbf{M}ulti-Question \textbf{R}easoning), which coordinates all questions about a video through one shared tool-use trajectory. At each round, a persistent policy model can invoke tools for one or more unresolved questions and submit answers for questions with sufficient evidence. Question-conditioned visual perception retrieves fine-grained clues for several questions in one call, while layered multi-question memory integrates reusable context into a shared video

translated_title: VAMR：面向高效长视频理解的多问题智能体推理
translated_abstract: 长视频理解通常涉及针对同一段录像不同方面的多个问题。然而，现有的视频智能体通常通过各自孤立的工具使用轨迹来处理每个问题。这会反复重启视频探索和记忆构建，错失了联合获取证据并逐步建立支持完整问题集合的共享理解的机会。我们提出了VAMR（Video Agent for Multi-Question Reasoning，多问题推理视频智能体），它通过一条共享的工具使用轨迹来协调针对同一视频的所有问题。在每一轮中，一个持久化的策略模型可以为一个或多个未解决的问题调用工具，并为已有足够证据的问题提交答案。问题条件化的视觉感知能够在一次调用中为多个问题检索细粒度线索，而分层多问题记忆则将可复用的上下文整合到共享的视频（记忆中）……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: VAMR通过单一共享的工具使用轨迹协同处理针对同一长视频的多个问题，结合问题条件化视觉感知与分层多问题记忆，避免逐问题独立探索的重复开销，实现高效的长视频理解。
en_tdlr: VAMR coordinates all questions about a long video through one shared tool-use trajectory, leveraging question-conditioned visual perception and layered multi-question memory to jointly gather evidence and build shared understanding, enabling efficient long-form video understanding.
